SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r1.claim: لا يذوقون may be circumstantial from the pronoun in آمنين.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا من الضمير في " آمنين " ، وأن يكون حالا ثالثة

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r2.claim: It may instead be a second or third circumstantial clause from the object of زوجناهم.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r2.anchor: حالاً ثالثة أو ثانية من مفعول " زوجناهم "

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r3.claim: آمنين may be circumstantial from the subject of يدعون, an adjective of that circumstantial, or an independent clause.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r3.anchor: و " آمنين " حال من فاعل " يدعون " كما تقدم، أو صفة ل " آمنين " أو مستأنف.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r4.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r4.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reads لا يذاقون in the passive.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r4.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن عبيد " لا يذاقون " مبنيا للمفعول.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r5.claim: One analysis makes the exception disconnected: they tasted the first death already, but will not taste death in Paradise.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r5.anchor: أنه منقطع أي: لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r6.claim: A connected exception is possible if, at worldly death, the believer is already in the station of Paradise through seeing its promise or certainty of its bliss.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r6.anchor: أنه متصل وتأولوه: بأن المؤمن عند موته في الدنيا بمنزلته في الجنة لمعاينة ما يعطاه منها، أو لما يتيقنه من نعيمها.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r7.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits an analysis in which إلا means سوى, “other than”; he considers it weak.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r7.anchor: أن " إلا " بمعنى سوى نقله الطبري وضعفه.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects al-Ṭabarī’s criticism: “other than” is a sound and coherent sense of إلا.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r8.anchor: " وليس تضعيفه بصحيح، بل هو كونها بمعنى سوى مستقيم متسق "

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r9.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī chooses a further sense for إلا: “after.”
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r9.anchor: أن " إلا " بمعنى بعد. واختاره الطبري، وأباه الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r10.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r10.claim: The majority reject “after” because this sense of إلا is not established.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r10.anchor: وأباه الجمهور؛ لأن " إلا " بمعنى بعد لم يثبت.

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the exception as an impossible condition: the past first death cannot be tasted in the future, so the phrase denies any taste of death in Paradise.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r11.anchor: أريد أن يقال: لا يذوقون فيها الموت البتة، فوضع قوله { إلا الموتة الأولى } موضع ذلك؛ لأن الموتة الماضية محال ذوقها في المستقبل

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r12.claim: Al-Samīn calls the device “negating a thing by its proof”: making an exception depend on an impossible case proves the negation.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r12.anchor: وهذا عند علماء البيان يسمى نفي الشيء بدليله. ومثله قول النابغة:

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r13.speaker: النابغة
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r13.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line similarly makes sword-notches an impossible “flaw,” thereby denying any flaw.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r13.anchor: لا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains the intended sense: they do not taste death there; their only death was experienced in this world.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r14.anchor: فبين أنه نفى عنهم ذوق الموت، وأنه لا ينالهم من ذلك غير ما تقدم في الدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r15.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r15.claim: The majority read ووقاهم without doubling.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r15.anchor: الجمهور على التخفيف. وقرأ أبو حيوة

SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r16.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r16.claim: Abū Ḥaywah doubles for emphasis, not causation, since the verb already takes two objects.
SAMIN-DURR:44:56/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة " ووقاهم " بالتشديد على المبالغة، ولا يكون للتعدية فإنه متعد إلى اثنين قبل ذلك.

ZAJJAJ:v4p428#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p428#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p428#2/r1.claim: They will never taste death in Paradise; the exception refers to the one death they already tasted in worldly life, as in the exception “except what has passed” in 4:22.
ZAJJAJ:v4p428#2/r1.anchor: المعنى لا يذوقون فيها الموت ألبتة سوى الموتة الأولى التي ذاقوها في الدنيا

ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r5.claim: In paradise they will not die again after their first, earthly death.
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r5.anchor: taste death there after having passed through their erstwhile death

ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r6.claim: God's favour preserves them from the blazing fire, which is the supreme triumph.
ASAD-NOTES:44:51/r6.anchor: all suffering through the blazing fire

ASAD-NOTES:44:51#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:51#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:51#n32/r1.claim: The exception means death beyond, or except for, the first and erstwhile death; compare 37:58-59.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r1.claim: The clause is either independent or circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r1.anchor: جملة مستأنفة أو حالية وكأنه أريد أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r2.claim: The intended sense is that they never taste death; naming the first death is hyperbolic because a past death cannot be tasted in the future.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r2.anchor: الموتة الماضية محال ذوقهافي المستقبل فهو من باب التعليقبال

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r3.claim: The paradox resembles telling someone who asks for water, “I will give you only embers”; Quran 4:22 similarly uses a connected exception for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r3.anchor: وقد علم أن الجمر لا يسقى ومثله قوله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r4.claim: The pronoun in “therein” refers to the gardens.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r4.anchor: وضمير ( فيها ) للجنات وقيل : هو متصل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r5.claim: On a connected exception, a believer at death sees what he will receive in Paradise as though already there, and thus seems to taste the first death there.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r5.anchor: المؤمن عند موته لمعاينة ما يعطاه في الجنة كأنه فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r6.claim: Another connected reading takes “therein” as the afterlife and death as its first state; al-Alusi objects that this fragments the construction and requires figurative language.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r6.anchor: للآخرة والموت أول أحوالها ولا يخفى ما فيه من التفكيك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r7.claim: A disconnected exception takes “therein” as Paradise: they tasted the first death in worldly life before entering it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r7.anchor: الضمير للجنات أي لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r8.claim: The exception is presumed connected unless an argument requires otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r8.anchor: والداعي لما سمعت من الأوجه دفع سؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r9.claim: The objection is that a worldly death in the past cannot be tasted later in Paradise; this follows only if exception from a negation affirms the excluded item in that setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r9.anchor: الموتة الأولى مما مضى لهم في الدنيا وما هو كذلك لا يمكن أني ذوقوه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r10.claim: If the exception instead means that they taste no death other than the first, the objection disappears because the first death is excluded from future deaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r10.anchor: والمعنى لا يذوقون سوى الموتة الأول من الموت فلاذ إشكال

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r11.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r11.claim: Al-Tabari takes إلا to mean “after”; most commentators do not recognize that sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r11.anchor: وقال الطبري : إلا بمعنى بعد والجمهور لم يثبتوا هذاالمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a view that إلا means سوى, “other than”; al-Tabari weakens it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r12.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى أن إلا بمعنى سوى وضعفه الطبري

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Tabari's objection: سوى gives a sound, coherent meaning and recalls their worldly state.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r13.anchor: ليس تضعيفه بصحيح بل يصح المعنى بسوى ويتسق

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r14.speaker: عبيد ابن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r14.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads the verb passively: “they are not made to taste.”
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r14.anchor: عبيد ابن عمير ( لا يذاقون ) مبنيا للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r15.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r15.claim: Abdullah's reading adds “the taste of death.”
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r15.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( لا يذوقون فيها طعم الموت )

ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r16.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r16.claim: A sound-chain report from Jabir says Paradise's people neither die nor sleep, since sleep is death's sibling.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p136#3/r16.anchor: بسند صحيح عن جابرابن عبد الله قال : قيل يا رأينا أهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p137/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137/r1.speaker: أبو حيوة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137/r1.claim: Abu Haywah doubles the qaf in وَوَقَّاهُمْ to intensify protection; the verb was already transitive, so the extra form adds meaning rather than transitivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137/r1.anchor: أبو حيوة ( ووقاهم ) مشدد القاف على المبالغة في التثكير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r3.claim: The exception means excepting the first death already tasted in worldly life; illa is used in the sense of apart from or after, as at 4:22.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r3.anchor: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى} أي سوى الموتة التي ذاقوها في الدنيا، وبعدها وضع: "إلا" موضع سوى وبعد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says the blessed meet the spirit and fragrant provision and see their Paradise homes at death, so their worldly death resembles being in Paradise through contact with its causes and vision of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنما استثنى الموتة الأولى وهي في الدنيا من موت في الجنة لأن السعداء حين يموتون يصيرون بلطف إلى أسباب الجنة، يلقون الروح والريحان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r5.claim: God protects them from the punishment of Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r8.claim: They live there forever; the exception may be disconnected or connected, with death as the first state of the afterlife, or the Garden as what believers approach and see at death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r8.anchor: والاستثناء منقطع أو متصل والضمير للآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r9.claim: Alternatively, the exception hyperbolically generalizes the negation: tasting the first death in the future is impossible.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r9.anchor: أو الاستثناء للمبالغة في تعميم النفي

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:53-56/r10.claim: A reading with doubled قاف intensifies “and He protected them.”

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r3.claim: In paradise, they will not experience even the onset or first taste of death again, let alone anything beyond it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r3.anchor: لا يتجدد لهم أوائل استطعامه فكيف بما وراء ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r4.claim: The exception reinforces the complete negation; the first death is mentioned because it already occurred and cannot happen again, so the exception is attached to an impossibility.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r4.anchor: وكان الاستثناء معيار العموم , وكان من المعلوم أن

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r5.claim: He says the location in paradise and the description first imply that death may be tasted again in hell; on the whole, paradise residents do not die, though some sinners may taste death outside it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r5.anchor: أن النار يذاق فيها الموت , والوصف بالأولى أن المذوق موتة ثانية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r6.claim: Alternatively, the first death was in a figurative paradise: believers have been in it during life through its causes and God’s decree, and some enjoy its blessings after death.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الموتة الأولى كانت في الجنة المجازية فلا يكون تعليقا بمحال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r7.claim: A prophetic report says that a believer visiting his brother remains in the harvest of paradise until he returns; asked what that harvest is, the Prophet answers, its fruits.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r7.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( المؤمن إذا عاد أخاه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r8.claim: The author also quotes the Prophet telling people who pass gardens of paradise to graze there, supporting the figurative sense of paradise’s present blessings.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r9.claim: He cites sound reports of posthumous enjoyment, including seeing and the food of martyrs, as evidence for those promised paradise already enjoying its blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r9.anchor: بما له من التمتع بالنظر ونحوه من الأكل للشهداء وغير ذلك مما ورد في الأخبار الصحيحة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p83/r10.claim: Their safety in paradise includes God’s protection from the punishment of hellfire.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r1.speaker: غير مسمى في المقتطف
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r1.claim: An unnamed fighter at Uhud cried that he could smell Paradise beyond the mountain, then fought until he was killed.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r1.anchor: قال يوم أحد : يا سعد بن معاذ الجنة ورب النضر إني لأجد ريحها من دون أحد , ثم قاتل حتى قتل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r2.claim: The full bliss of Paradise will be completed after the resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r2.anchor: ثم يكون تمام ذلك النعيم بالجنة بعد البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r3.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r3.claim: Ibn Burjān calls worldly life a small paradise for the mindful believer because God cares for, draws near to, regards, remembers, and accompanies them in worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r3.anchor: قال ابن برجان : الدنيا إذا تحققت في حق المؤمن المتقي وتتبع النظر فيها فإنها جنة صغرى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r4.claim: God protects the community of the pious from Hell as recompense for their piety.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r4.anchor: ولما كان السياق للمتقين قال : { ووقاهم } أي جملة المتقين في جزاء ما اتقوه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r5.claim: Sinners God wills to admit to Hell are punished according to their sins, die there until intercession is allowed, then leave and are revived by the water of life.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r5.anchor: وأما غير المتقين من العصاة فيدخل الله من أراد منهم النار فيعذر كلا منهم على قدر ذنوبه ثم يمتهم فيها ويستمرون إلى أن يأذن الله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r6.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet distinguishing permanent denizens of Fire, who neither die nor live, from sinful Muslims; al-Dārimī adds that they burn proportionally to their sins, become charcoal, then leave after intercession and regrow by Paradise's rivers.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r7.claim: Abū Yaʿlā transmits from Anas that the Prophet said people enter the Fire until charcoal, then enter Paradise and are identified as the people of Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r7.anchor: وروى أبو يعلى عن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( يدخل ناس في النار حتى إذا صاروا فحما أدخلوا الجنة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r8.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says that after crossing the Bridge, believers intercede for their brothers and, with God's permission, remove them from Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r8.anchor: ولأحمد بن منيع عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( يوضع الصراط ) فذكر شفاعة المؤمنين في إخوانهم بعد جواز

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r9.speaker: الغافر الفارسي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r9.claim: Al-Ghāfir al-Fārisī glosses ḍabāʾir as the plural of ḍabārah, meaning groups of people.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85/r9.anchor: الضبائر قال بعد الغافر الفارسي في مجمع الرغائب : جمع ضبارة مثل عمارة عمائر : جماعات الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r1.claim: The continuation of Abū Saʿīd's report says believers take the rescued people from Hell, cast them into the water of life, and they grow like plants amid flood debris.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r1.anchor: قال : ( فيخرجونهم منها فيطرحونهم في ماء الحياة فينبتون نبات الزرع في غثاء السيل )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿUmar transmits from ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr that the Prophet describes charred people regrowing in the river of life at Paradise's gate and being welcomed as those freed by the Merciful.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r2.anchor: ولابن أبي عمر عن عبيد بن عمير رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يخرج الله قوما من النار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r3.claim: The gloss explains al-thaʿāyir as a plant resembling asparagus.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r3.anchor: الثعاير - بالثاء المثلثة والعين والراء المهملتين : نبات كالهليون

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhī grades a report from Jābir ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ: monotheists burned to charcoal are shown mercy, sprinkled with water at Paradise's gates, regrow, and enter Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r4.anchor: وروى الترمذي - وقال : حسن صحيح - وروي من غر وجه عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r8.claim: This added circumstantial clause promises everlasting blessing, since death ends worldly enjoyment; likewise, saying the associators do not die warns of everlasting punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r8.anchor: وجملة { لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى } حال أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r9.claim: The exception affirms the negation by mentioning what seems its opposite: they never taste death at all, as confirmed by calling it the first death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r9.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا الموتة الأولى } من تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r10.claim: Al-ūlā means the death that came before, as in the earlier statement that they have only their first death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r10.anchor: والمراد ب { الأولى } السالفة ، كما تقدم آنفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r11.claim: Protection from Hell is a blessing to recall with gratitude; one should thank God when seeing another in distress or hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r11.anchor: وذلك مما يحمد الله عليه كما ورد أن من آداب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r12.claim: The pronoun in waqāhum returns to the first-person pronoun in zawwajnāhum by a shift in grammatical person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p319/r12.anchor: وضمير { وقاهم } عائد إلى ضمير المتكلم في { وزوجناهم }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r1.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r1.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj take illa to mean “apart from”: the people of Paradise taste no death other than the death they experienced in this world.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the fortunate who die see their Paradise dwellings and its blessings, so their worldly death is as if they had died in Paradise because they are already connected to and see it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r2.anchor: وإذا ماتوا في الدنيا فكأنهم ماتوا في الجنة لا تصالهم بأسبابها ومشاهدتهم إياها قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir takes illa to mean “after,” as in one interpretation of 4:22.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r3.anchor: كما ذكرنا في أحد الوجوه في قوله ﴿ إلا ما قد سلف ﴾ النساء 22 وهذا قول ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r2.claim: The exception is disconnected and reinforces the negation: the people of Paradise will never taste death there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r2.anchor: هذا استثناء يؤكد النفي، فإنه استثناء منقطع ومعناه: أنهم لا يذوقون فيها الموت أبدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r3.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says death will be brought as a speckled ram and slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, then each group is told it will have no more death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r3.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يؤتى بالموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r4.claim: Abu Said and Abu Hurayra report the Prophet's promise that Paradise's people will have lasting health, life, ease, and youth without sickness, death, hardship, or aging; Muslim transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة، رضي الله عنهما، قالا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that whoever fears God enters Paradise to enjoy life without death, worn-out clothes, or fading youth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r6.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said people in Paradise do not sleep because sleep is the sibling of death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r6.anchor: عن جابر، رضي الله عنه، قال: سئل نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أينام أهل الجنة؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r7.claim: Iraqis and Abu Ishaq call the transmitter Abu Muslim al-Agharr, while Medinans call him Abu Abd Allah al-Agharr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p261#2/r7.anchor: هكذا يقول أبو إسحاق وأهل العراق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r1.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bazzar transmit Jabir's report that Paradise's people do not sleep; al-Bazzar says only al-Thawri narrated it from Ibn al-Munkadir and only al-Firyabi from al-Thawri, though Ibn Kathir notes another route above.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن المنكدر، عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r2.claim: Along with abiding bliss, God shields the people of Paradise from Hell's painful depths; they attain what they seek and escape what they fear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p262/r2.anchor: قد وقاهم، وسلمهم ونجاهم وزحزحهم من

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r4.claim: The pronoun in 'therein' refers to the gardens.

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r5.claim: Mawt and mawta are verbal nouns from one verb, but mawta denotes a single instance while mawt denotes the genus; negating even one instance emphatically excludes any death.
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r5.anchor: الموت والموتة : مصدران من فعل واحد كالنفخ والنفخة

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r6.claim: The exception is disconnected: paradise dwellers taste no death there, while the single death they already tasted was before entering paradise; al-Baḥr al-ʿUlūm glosses this as tasting nothing of death.
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r6.anchor: والاستثناء منقطع ؛ أي : لا يذوقون الموت في الجنة

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r7.claim: After resurrection and entry to paradise they continue in eternal life; unlike the people of the Fire, who neither die nor live, paradise has no aging, sleep, fear, day or night, darkness, heat, cold, or exit.
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r7.anchor: ثم إذا بعثوا ودخلوا الجنة يستمرون على الحياة

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r8.claim: An unattributed saying lists ten things absent from paradise: aging, sleep, death, fear, night, day, darkness, heat, cold, and departure.
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r8.anchor: ليس فيها هرم ولا نوم ولا موت ولا خوف

BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the exception is connected and states an impossible condition: tasting the past first death in the future, as in the exception in 4:22; this cannot occur in paradise, the abode of life.
BURSEVI:v8p333#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا على أن المراد بيان استحالة ذوق الموت فيها

BURSEVI:v8p334/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334/r1.claim: Wiqāya is protecting something from harm; God protects the blessed from the Fire and wards its punishment away from them.
BURSEVI:v8p334/r1.anchor: الوقاية حفظ الشيء مما يؤذيه ويضره ؛ أي : حفظهم من النار

BURSEVI:v8p334/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334/r2.claim: Ishārī allusion: the punishment of the blazing Fire also signifies the torment of distance from God and abandonment.
BURSEVI:v8p334/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى عذاب البعد وجحيم الهجران

MUQATIL:44:51-57/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:44:51-57/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:44:51-57/r6.claim: They never taste death in Paradise, apart from the first death they experienced in worldly life; the Lord protects them from Hell's punishment.
MUQATIL:44:51-57/r6.anchor: أبدا { إلا الموتة الأولى } التى كانت فى الدنيا، { ووقاهم } ، يعنى الرب تعالى، { عذاب الجحيم }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r1.claim: In Paradise they never taste death; illa al-mawtata al-ūlā means except for, or apart from, the first death they tasted in worldly life. Another construal is but they already tasted that death in the world.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يذوقون فيها ﴾ اى في الجنة ﴿ الموت ﴾ البته ﴿ إلا الموتة الأولى ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128/r2.claim: God protected them from the punishment of Hell.

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r1.claim: They will never taste death there because they remain forever; the exception is disconnected, since the first death was experienced in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r1.anchor: أي لا يذوقون فيها الموت ألبتة لأنهم خالدون فيها. ثم قال: { إلا الموتة الأولى } على الاستثناء المنقطع

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r2.claim: Sibawayh adduces poetry as an example of a disconnected exception, where what follows إلا is not part of what precedes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r2.anchor: وأنشد سيبويه: من كان أسرع في تفرق فالج فلبونه جربت معا وأغدت

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r3.claim: Another interpretation gives إلا the sense of after, while a further one takes it as excepting the first death they experienced in the world, like the cited marriage prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن «إلا» بمعنى بعد كقولك: ما كلمت رجلا اليوم إلا رجلا عندك، أي بعد رجل عندك

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r4.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r4.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the exception is valid because, as a believer approaches death, angels of mercy meet him with spirit and fragrance, and his death is associated with Paradise through the causes he acquired.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r4.anchor: وقال القتبي: «إلا الموتة الأولى» معناه أن المؤمن إذا أشرف على الموت استقبلته ملائكة الرحمة ويلقى الروح والريحان

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r5.claim: Death is an accident and cannot literally be tasted; the verse metaphorically compares it to food whose taste one dislikes.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r5.anchor: والموت عرض لا يذاق، ولكن جعل كالطعام الذي يكره ذوقه، فاستعير فيه لفظ الذوق

QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r6.claim: God's protection from Hell is a gracious favor to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:56-57/r6.anchor: أي فعل ذلك بهم تفضلا منه عليهم

QASHANI:44:55-57/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:44:55-57/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:44:55-57/r2.claim: The first death is bodily nature; it does not exclude voluntary annihilation of acts, attributes, and Essence, since each such death is a purer and more delightful life, each in its own garden.
QASHANI:44:55-57/r2.anchor: أي: الطبيعة الجسمانية لا الفناء من الأفعال والصفات والذات فإن كل فناء منها وإن كان موتا إراديا

QASHANI:44:55-57/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:44:55-57/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:44:55-57/r3.claim: God protects them from the hell of deprivation arising from a remaining residue, much less from the hell of bodily nature.
QASHANI:44:55-57/r3.anchor: أي: جحيم الحرمان بوجود البقية فضلا عن الخذلان في جحيم الطبيعة

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r2.claim: After describing their pleasures and comforts, God states that their life in paradise is everlasting.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r2.anchor: ولما وصف الله تعالى أنواع ما هم فيه من الخيرات والراحات ، بين أن حياتهم دائمة

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the exception as an impossible counterfactual: a past death cannot be tasted in the future, so they never die there.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r3.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) أريد أن يقال : لا يذوقون فيها الموت البتة فوضع قوله { إلا الموتة الاولى }

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r4.claim: Another explanation takes illā as meaning but: they do not taste death there, but they have already tasted the first death.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r4.anchor: أن إلا بمعنى لكن والتقدير لا يذوقون فيها الموت لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r5.claim: Rāzī presents true paradise as the soul's joy in knowing, obeying, and loving God; one may experience it in worldly life, so the exception recalls the first death after that spiritual experience.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r5.anchor: الثالث : أن الجنة حقيقتها ابتهاج النفس وفرحها بمعرفة الله تعالى وبطاعته ومحبته

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r6.claim: Rāzī cites a saying attributed to the Prophet that God's prophets do not die but are moved from one abode to another, supporting the spiritual account.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r6.anchor: ولهذا السبب قال عليه السلام : ( أنبياء الله لا يموتون ولكن ينقلون من دار إلى دار )

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r7.claim: A further explanation treats tasting as experience: since knowledge can be called taste, recalling a death can also be called tasting it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r7.anchor: وإذا صح أن يسمى العلم بالذوق صح أن يسمى تذكره أيضا بالذوق

RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r8.claim: Although people in hell also do not die, the glad tidings concern eternal life after the people of paradise have already received all those blessings and joys.
RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r8.anchor: أن البشارة ما وقعت بدوام الحياة مع سابقة حصول تلك الخيرات والسعادات فظهر الفرق

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r1.claim: Rāzī notes a reading that pronounces wa-waqqāhum with a doubled qāf.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r1.anchor: قرىء ووقاهم بالتشديد ، فإن قالوا مقتضى الدليل أن يكون ذكر الوقاية

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r2.claim: Though protection from hell would logically be mentioned before winning paradise, Rāzī explains the order as meaning that God protected them from hell at the outset.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r2.anchor: التقدير كأنه تعالى قال : ووقاهم في أول الأمر عن عذاب الجحيم

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r3.claim: Rāzī's school argues that all the rewards just enumerated come through God's favor and generosity, not as an entitlement earned against Him.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r3.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن الثواب يحصل تفضلا من الله تعالى لا بطريق الاستحقاق

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī says people may earn most of these rewards through deeds, yet they remain God's favor because He graciously imposed the duties leading to them, like giving someone money to acquire an estate.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أكثر ههذ الأشياء وإن كانوا قد استحقوه بعملهم فهو بفضل الله لأنه تعالى تفضل بالتكليف

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r5.claim: Rāzī rejects al-Qāḍī's account: if reward is an obligation on God whose omission would imply folly and denial of divinity, it cannot be called a favor.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r5.anchor: قلنا مذهبك أن هذا الثواب حق لازم على الله ، وأنه تعالى لو أخل به لصار سفيها ولخرج به عن الإلهية

STUDYQURAN:44:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r1.speaker: Q, R, Z
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r1.claim: The reverent experience only worldly physical death and have no death in Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r1.anchor: The reverent experience only the physical death of this world and experience no death in Paradise (Q, R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:44:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r2.claim: The reverent are spared afterlife punishment, while disbelievers undergo it continually as if repeatedly dying.
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r2.anchor: They will be spared the punishment of the Hereafter, but the disbelievers will experience it continually

STUDYQURAN:44:56/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r3.claim: Their not tasting death contrasts with the disbelievers’ claim in verse 35 that they will taste only one death.
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r3.anchor: that the reverent taste not death stands in contrast to the claim posed by the disbelievers in v. 35

STUDYQURAN:44:56/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r4.claim: Protection from Hellfire expresses Divine Mercy, which precedes the Divine Wrath.
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r4.anchor: integral to the Mercy of the Divine Nature, which precedes God’s Wrath

STUDYQURAN:44:56/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r5.speaker: The Prophet
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r5.claim: After Companions say a mother would protect her child from fire, the Prophet says God is more tender toward His servants.
STUDYQURAN:44:56/r5.anchor: The Prophet then said, “And God is more tender toward His servants than is this woman toward her child.”

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r1.claim: The people of Paradise will not taste death there after the first death they experienced in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r1.anchor: {لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى} [الدخان: 56]

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r2.claim: Some Arabic grammarians read illa as meaning other than, comparing the construction with 4:22.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r2.anchor: {لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى} [الدخان: 56]

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r3.claim: Reading illa as other than would imply that the blessed taste another death, although God has secured Paradise's inhabitants from death after entering it.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r3.anchor: وجب أن يكون قد أثبت بقوله: {إلا الموتة الأولى} [الدخان: 56] موتة من نوع الأولى هم ذائقوها

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r4.claim: Here illa stands in place of after because their meanings draw close in this construction, yielding no death after the first one.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r4.anchor: وضعت «إلا» في موضع «بعد» لما نصف من تقارب معنى «إلا»

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r5.claim: Arab usage can substitute illa for baʿda when the two expressions have sufficiently close meanings.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r5.anchor: فبعد، وإلا: متقاربتا المعنى في هذا الموضع

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r6.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r6.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb uses rajāʾ to mean fear: the bitten person did not fear another sting.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r6.anchor: قال في ذلك أبو ذؤيب: إذا لسعته الدبر لم يرج لسعها

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r7.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses zannū for certainty or knowledge reached by report rather than direct sight.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r7.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: فقلت لهم ظنوا بألفي مدجج

TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r8.claim: In 4:22, illa likewise means after what the fathers had done in the pre-Islamic period, rather than other than it.
TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r8.anchor: إنما معناه: بعد الذي سلف منكم في الجاهلية

SULAMI:v2p238#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p238#5/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p238#5/r1.claim: Junayd says the people of Paradise do not subsist through God's own uncreated subsistence; rather, they are made to subsist by it, since only God has eternally remained and will remain in truth.
SULAMI:v2p238#5/r1.anchor: قلت للجنيد رحمة الله عليه : أهل الجنة باقين ببقاء الحق ؟ فقال : لا ولكنهم مبقون ببقاء الحق والباقي على الحقيقة لم يزل ولا يزال باقيا

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r2.claim: The people of the everlasting Garden have eternal life and are never overtaken by death.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r2.anchor: في جنة الخلد أحياء بحياة أبدية لا يعتريها موت

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r3.claim: The apparent exception seems to say they taste the first death in Paradise, contrary to the intended meaning.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r3.anchor: والمراد خلافه قطعا، وبتقرير آخر الموتة الأولى هي موتة الدنيا

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r4.claim: A further problem is that the first death occurred in the past, so it cannot straightforwardly be excepted from a future denial.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r4.anchor: والتلبس في المستقبل بأمر ماض محال قطعا فما معنى استثناء الموتة الأولى

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r5.claim: There are two deaths between worldly life and the Hour: transition to barzakh and then from barzakh to the afterlife; why omit the second?
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r5.anchor: أن بين الحياة الدنيا والساعة موتتين موتة بالانتقال من الدنيا إلى البرزخ وموتة بالانتقال من البرزخ إلى الآخرة

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r6.claim: One answer treats the exception as disconnected: they already tasted the first death in the world; the general denial remains intact.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r6.anchor: لكنهم قد ذاقوا الموتة الأولى في الدنيا وقد مضت

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r7.claim: Another answer reads illā as ‘other than’ and makes ‘the first death’ an appositive, not an exception.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r7.anchor: والمعنى لا يذوقون فيها سوى الموتة الأولى من الموت أما الموتة الأولى

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r8.claim: Neither explanation accounts for calling it the first death; prior discussion is at 44:35.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r8.anchor: بأن شيئا من الوجهين لا يوجه اتصاف الموتة بالأولى

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r9.claim: For the second objection, take illā as ‘other than’ and the phrase as apposition: death in barzakh and in the Garden is denied, while the worldly death is past.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r9.anchor: كانت الآية مسوقة لنفي غير الموتة الأولى وهي الموتة الثانية التي هي موتة البرزخ

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r10.claim: Wiqāya means guarding something from harm; God protected them from the punishment of Hell.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r10.anchor: الوقاية حفظ الشيء مما يؤذيه ويضره

TABATABAI:44:55-56/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r11.claim: The clauses complete the division of hardships: death changes abode or state, while Hell changes happiness into misery.
TABATABAI:44:55-56/r11.anchor: تتميم لقسمة المكاره أي إنهم مصونون من الانتقال من دار إلى دار ومن نشأة الجنة إلى نشأة غيرها

TABRISI:44:51-59/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:51-59/r10.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:44:51-59/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the first death as an exception meaning “other than” the death tasted in this world, comparing it with another Qur'anic exception.
TABRISI:44:51-59/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج: معناه سوى الموتة التي ذاقوها في الدنيا

TABRISI:44:51-59/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:51-59/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:51-59/r11.claim: Al-Tabrisi says “other than” is an adverb while illa is a particle; he prefers parsing illa and what follows as an adjective or substitute meaning ghayr, since the first death is past.
TABRISI:44:51-59/r11.anchor: وأقول إن سوى لا يكون إلا ظرفا وإلا حرف فكيف يكون بمعناه فالأولى أن يكون إلا هنا مع ما بعدها صفة أو بدلا بمعنى غير

TABRISI:44:56-59/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r2.claim: Death is likened to unpleasant food that one tastes, then denied for Paradise's people.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r2.anchor: شبه الموت بالطعام الذي يذاق ويتكره عند المذاق ثم نفى أن يكون ذلك في الجنة

TABRISI:44:56-59/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r3.claim: Though all afterlife inhabitants avoid death, this reassurance singles out the blessed to promise pleasant life; those enduring deathlike punishment undergo repeated deaths from torment.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r3.anchor: مع أن جميع أهل الآخرة لا يذوقون الموت لما في ذلك من البشارة لهم بالحياة الهنيئة في الجنة

TABRISI:44:56-59/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:44:56-59/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the exception to mean “after the first death.”

TABRISI:44:56-59/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:44:56-59/r5.claim: Another interpretation means that they have already tasted the first death.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها

TABRISI:44:56-59/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r6.claim: The remaining interpretation means “other than the first death”; al-Tabrisi's grammatical explanation is in the preceding segment.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r6.anchor: وقيل: سوى الموتة الأولى وقد بينا ما عندنا فيه

TABRISI:44:56-59/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r7.claim: God keeps them away from the punishment of the Fire.

TABRISI:44:56-59/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
TABRISI:44:56-59/r8.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that a sinful believer cannot leave Hell, since this verse says the saved people are protected from the Fire.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r8.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذا على أن الفاسق الملي لا يخرج من النار

TABRISI:44:56-59/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r9.claim: It may concern those who do not deserve entry, those pardoned despite deserving it, or protection forever or from the kind of torment reserved for unbelievers.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r9.anchor: والجواب عن ذلك أن هذه الآية يجوز أن تكون مختصة بمن لا يستحق دخول النار فلا يدخلها

FARRA:v3p44/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p44/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p44/r1.claim: فضلا means God did this graciously; it could also be nominative, meaning That is a favor from your Lord.
FARRA:v3p44/r1.anchor: وقوله: ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم (56) فضلا (57) . أي فعله تفضلا منه، وهو مما لو جاء رفعا لكان صوابا أي: ذلك فضل من ربك.

THALABI:v8p356/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p356/r1.speaker: أبو قرصافة
THALABI:v8p356/r1.claim: Abu Qursafa reports the Prophet saying that removing rubbish from a mosque is a dowry for the houris; no grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p356/r1.anchor: عن عزة بنت أبي قرصافة، عن أبيها قال: سمعت رسول الله

THALABI:v8p356/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p356/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p356/r3.claim: The exception means after the first death: illa stands in place of baʿda, as in 4:22, and like saying one has eaten no food today except what one ate yesterday.
THALABI:v8p356/r3.anchor: يعني سوى الموتة الأولى وبعدها وضع (إلا) موضع بعد كقوله: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم

THALABI:v8p356/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p356/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p356/r4.claim: God's protection of the people of Paradise from Hell's punishment is a favor from Him and the great triumph.
THALABI:v8p356/r4.anchor: ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم فضلا من ربك ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r1.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r1.claim: The scholars of meaning call “tasting” death metaphorical: it is enduring the pains and causes that bring death, while death itself is an accident that cannot literally be tasted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r1.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: جعل الموت في مقاساة الآلام والأسباب التي يحدث عندها الموت،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r2.claim: The promise of no death heightens the joy of Paradise's pleasant life; in Hell, repeated death from suffering is withheld, increasing anguish and distress.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r2.anchor: إن أهل الجنة في حياة هنيئة بشارتهم بالخلود تزيدهم سرورا وقرة عين، وأهل النار يموتون موتات كثيرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the excepted first death as the death experienced in this world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: التي كانت في الدنيا (¬5)، وقال مقاتل: يعني: المرة الأولى التي كانت في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi reads illā as “other than”: they experience no death in Paradise beyond the first death they had in the world, paralleling 4:22.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r4.anchor: الموت البتة سوى الموتة الأولى التي ذاقوها في الدنيا، وهذا كما قال (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra compares the exception to an expression where illā adds to what came before rather than subtracting from it, as in this verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r5.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الفراء قال: ومثله في الكلام: لك عندي ألف إلا مالك عندي من قبل فلان،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r6.claim: Some scholars of meaning take illā to mean “after,” yielding “after the first death.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: (إلا) بمعنى: بعد، أي: بعد الموتة الأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r7.speaker: بعض
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r7.claim: Another view takes illā to mean “but”: they have tasted the first death, but no further death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r7.anchor: وقيل (إلا) بمعنى: لكن، كأنه قيل: لكن الموتة الأولى (¬2)، وقد ذاقوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the worldly death can be excepted from their state in Paradise because the blessed encounter its comfort and see their dwellings and open gates at death, already connected to Paradise's causes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p126#2/r8.anchor: وذكر ابن قتيبة وجها حسنا فقال: إنما استثنى الموتة الأولى وهي في الدنيا، من موت في الجنة؛

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p404#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p404#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p404#2/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says this phrase is explained in his Kitāb Taʾwīl al-Mushkil.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:53-56/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:53-56/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:53-56/r5.claim: The only death they have tasted is the first death they experienced in worldly life; they do not die in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:53-56/r5.anchor: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا } سوى { الموتة الأولى } الموتة التي ذاقوها في الدنيا

ELMALILI:44:56-57/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:44:56-57/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:44:56-57/r1.claim: Because disbelievers say in al-Muʾmin 40:11 that God caused them to die twice, the God-fearing have no death after the first one—not in the barzakh or the Hereafter.

BURHAN:v3p47/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p47/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p47/r1.claim: A statement can be cast as an impossible condition to intensify its full negation: as a camel cannot pass through a needle’s eye, the deniers will never enter Paradise, and the endpoint has no actual limit.
BURHAN:v3p47/r1.anchor: إبراز الكلام في صورة المستحيل على طريق المبالغة ليدل على بقية جمله كقول العرب لا أكلمك حتى يبيض القار وحتى يشيب الغراب

BURHAN:v3p47/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p47/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p47/r2.claim: The camel-through-needle expression means the people will not enter Paradise at all; because the impossible condition never occurs, the negative has no endpoint.
BURHAN:v3p47/r2.anchor: يعنى والجمل لا يلج في السم فهؤلاء لا يدخلون فهو في المعنى متعلق بالحال فالمعنى أنهم لا يدخلون الجنة أصلا

BURHAN:v3p47/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p47/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p47/r3.claim: A poet exaggerates emaciation beyond the Qur’anic example, but Zarkashi says such poetic hyperbole does not permit attempts to match the Qur’an.
BURHAN:v3p47/r3.anchor: وهذا على طريقة الشعراء في اعتبار المبالغة وإلا فمعارضات القرآن لا تجوز كما سبق التنبيه عليه

BURHAN:v3p47/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p47/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p47/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the apparent exception as emphatic: they cannot experience the first death again, so they experience no death in Paradise; the exception alludes to that impossibility.
BURHAN:v3p47/r7.anchor: ووجهة الزمخشري 4 بأنه من التوكيد في الدلالة والموتة الأولى

BURHAN:v3p48/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p48/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p48/r1.claim: If the exception is disconnected, the meaning is ‘but they have already tasted the first death.’ This is one of the proposed explanations of the apparent exception.
BURHAN:v3p48/r1.anchor: هذا إن جعلنا الاستثناء متصلا فإن كان منقطعا فالمعنى لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها

BURHAN:v3p48/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p48/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p48/r2.claim: If the exception is connected, ‘in it’ can mean in the preliminaries of Paradise: a dying person who sees their station there is treated as already being there, with ‘tasting’ used figuratively as an impossible event.
BURHAN:v3p48/r2.anchor: ويحتمل على الاتصال أن يكون المعنى فيها أي في مقدماتها لأن الذي يرى مقامه في الجنة عند الجنة عند موته ينزل منزلة من هو فيها بتأويل الذوق

BURHAN:v3p48/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p48/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p48/r3.claim: Zarkashi totals three explanations: al-Zamakhshari’s emphatic connected exception, the disconnected ‘already tasted’ reading, and a connected reading referring to Paradise’s preliminaries.
BURHAN:v3p48/r3.anchor: فالمعنى لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها ويحتمل على الاتصال أن يكون المعنى فيها

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r5.claim: One possible reading of “their first deaths” is the two past deaths, in the world and in the intermediate realm, since both have become prior events.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r5.anchor: “İlk ölümleri” ifadesinden, her ikisi de gelip geçtiği ve “önceki” niteliğini aldığı için “dünyada ve berzahta vuku bulan iki ölüm” kastedilmiş olabilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r6.claim: The stronger reading is death at the end of worldly life, because the passage contrasts the temporary world with eternity and mortal life with life without death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r6.anchor: bize daha güçlü gelen ihtimal, dünya hayatının sonundaki ölümün kastedilmiş olmasıdır. Çünkü burada dünya ile âhiret, geçici ile ebedî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r7.claim: Whichever reading is adopted, the verse says people die once at the end of worldly life, not repeatedly die and return; it therefore rejects reincarnation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r7.anchor: insanların defalarca ölüp dirileceklerini değil, dünya hayatı sonunda bir kere öleceklerini ifade eden âyet, reenkarnasyon inancını da reddetmiş olmaktadır

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r1.claim: In the exception, إلا means سوى, apart from; the same usage occurs in the rule about marriages from before prohibition.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r1.anchor: فإن (إلا) في هذا الموضع أيضا بمعنى (سوى)

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r2.claim: The first death is worldly; afterward the blessed enter differing means of Paradise by God's grace, proportionate to rank, including spirit and fragrance, an opened gate, or martyr spirits in green birds.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r2.anchor: لأن السعداء حين يموتون يصيرون بما شاء الله من لطفه وقدرته، إلى أسباب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r3.claim: The cited poet uses تعلق to mean eat, describing martyrs' spirits feeding in green birds in Paradise.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r3.anchor: تعلق في الجنة. أي تأكل، قال الشاعر :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r5.claim: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib is described as the two-winged figure flying with the angels in Paradise.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r5.anchor: وجعفر بن أبي طالب ذو الجناحين يطير مع الملائكة في الجنة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p26/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p26/r5.speaker: الطاعنون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p26/r5.claim: They object that worldly death cannot be excepted from remaining in Paradise, comparing it to excluding yesterday's gift from today's giving.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p26/r5.anchor: كيف يستثنى موتا كان في الدنيا من مكثهم في الجنة؟ وهل يجوز أن يقال في الكلام

NAHHAS:v4p136/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p136/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p136/r8.claim: The exception is accusative because it is not from the same category as what precedes it.
NAHHAS:v4p136/r8.anchor: نصب لأنه استثناء ليس من الأول

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.claim: The passage presents intellectual and historical evidence for reward and punishment, then depicts the fates of believers and disbelievers; God treats them differently with complete justice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.anchor: logical as well as historical arguments in favour of reward and punishment are briefly referred to. It is mentioned in detail that God will not deal equally between those who spent their lives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.claim: The coming section identifies disbelief in life after death as the cause of Quraysh rebellion and heedlessness of the future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.anchor: the real reason for the rebelliousness of the Quraysh is highlighted: they do not imagine that there is life after this worldly existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.claim: The section first offers intellectual and natural arguments for reward and punishment, then describes the fate of believers and disbelievers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.anchor: first the intellectual and natural arguments which substantiate the law of reward and punishment are cited. After this, the fate of both the believers and the disbelievers is depicted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p244/r12.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p244/r12.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p244/r12.claim: The fruit will not diminish or be withheld, and they will have no fear of death; they are shielded from every fear and enjoy eternal bliss.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p244/r12.anchor: They will be shielded from all fears and enjoy eternal bliss.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r1.claim: The word first means their worldly death is the only death they will taste; their life and pleasure thereafter are abiding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r1.anchor: after the death they tasted in this world, they will never taste it again

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r2.claim: Their Lord frees them from death and Hell; this special divine favour is the supreme triumph.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r2.anchor: This is a special favour to them by the Prophet’s Lord, and this, in reality, is the supreme triumph

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r1.claim: The past first death cannot be tasted in the future; it is excepted as the death already experienced in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r1.anchor: لأن الموتة الماضية محال ذوقها في المستقبل، فإنهم يذوقونها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r2.speaker: ابن عطية والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some take illā as “other than”; al-Ṭabarī weakens this and understands it as “after.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: قدر قوم إلا بسوى، وضعف ذلك الطبري وقدرها ببعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Ṭabarī's objection: “other than” is sound, and the verse denies any death beyond the one already undergone in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r3.anchor: وليس تضعيفه بصحيح، بل يصح المعنى بسوى ويتسق. وأما معنى الآية، فتبين أنه نفى عنهم ذوق الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayya reads the verb with a doubled qāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: ووقاهم، مشددا بالقاف

DAMGHANI:v1p35/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r3.claim: The resumptive exception construction also appears in the statement that they taste no death except the first death, and in several other sūras.
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r3.anchor: لا يذوقون فيها موت إلا الموتة الأولى
